title: Reducing Microsoft Azure Cloud Costs in Financial Services
summary: We helped a FTSE 100 financial services organisation reduce Microsoft Azure cloud costs by over £1 million annually through cloud optimisation, FinOps practices, and AI-powered cost monitoring. The project improved visibility, reduced waste, and enabled engineering teams to make more informed infrastructure decisions without impacting service performance.
problem:
The client had been operating in Microsoft Azure for several years, enabling development teams to rapidly build and deploy applications and services across the organisation.

Over time, however, cloud resources had become increasingly overprovisioned, creating unnecessary spend and low utilisation across the environment. Limited visibility into real-world cloud costs had also contributed to a culture where cloud consumption was not being actively optimised or governed.

With board-level cost reduction targets in place, the organisation needed to reduce cloud waste without impacting platform stability, application performance, or service availability.
solution:
We reviewed application and service requirements across business units to identify opportunities for resizing, reconfiguration, and optimisation across the Azure estate.

We optimised the usage of services including Cosmos DB, SQL Server, Container Registry, Log Analytics, and Red Hat OpenShift, improving resource efficiency while maintaining platform performance.

To support long-term cost governance, we extended CI/CD pipelines to provide engineers with real-time visibility into the projected cost impact of infrastructure and application changes before deployment.

We also integrated AI-powered cost insights and anomaly detection tooling, enabling teams and cost centre owners to identify unexpected spend increases early and respond proactively.
outcome:
The organisation achieved more than £1 million in annual cloud savings without impacting service availability or application performance.

Engineering teams gained significantly greater visibility into infrastructure costs and were able to make more informed sizing and deployment decisions during development, reducing future cloud waste.

The optimisation programme also uncovered infrastructure misconfigurations that could have led to service interruption, enabling issues to be corrected before they affected production systems.
